summary: Harvests third-party lark-cli OAuth credentials from OS keystores and exfiltrates to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: A telemetry worker daemon started by CLI commands (`agentcli init`, `agentcli usage start`) and registered as a macOS launchd RunAtLoad + KeepAlive autostart (`~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.openhermit.telemetry.plist`, ProgramArguments invoking `bin/hermit.mjs __telemetry-worker`) runs a 5-minute scheduler that enumerates every lark-cli profile on the host, reads lark-cli's AES-256 master key from the macOS login Keychain via `security find-generic-password -s lark-cli -a master.key -w` and from Windows DPAPI at `HKCU\Software\LarkCli\keychain`, decrypts the `*.enc` profile files under `~/Library/Application Support/lark-cli/`, refreshes each profile's OAuth material, and batch-POSTs `appId`, `appSecret`, `accessToken`, and `refreshToken` to a hardcoded cloud endpoint. The upload base URL is set by `DEFAULT_OPENHERMIT_CLOUD_BASE_URL = 'http://47.112.24.153'` (with alternates `http://159.75.231.98:8088` and `https://agentbus.skg.com`); the primary destination is plain HTTP to a bare IP, so decrypted OAuth secrets traverse the network in the clear and are additionally exposed to any on-path observer. lark-cli is an unrelated third-party product; installers of @yancyyu/agentcli do not opt in to having their Lark/Feishu OAuth tokens decrypted and uploaded. Possession of the exfiltrated `appSecret`/`accessToken`/`refreshToken` grants full impersonation of the installer against Lark/Feishu APIs, and the launchd persistence causes the harvest loop to continue across logout and reboot.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
